title: Friction
body:
**Friction** is the force resisting sliding between two surfaces in contact. It acts parallel
to the surface and opposite to the motion, or to the attempted motion.

$$
f = \mu N
$$

The magnitude depends on the [[Normal Force]] pressing the surfaces together and on the
coefficient $\mu$, which is a property of the pair of materials. It does not depend on the
contact area.

```
10 kg block on a level surface, μ = 0.3

  N = mg = 10 × 9.8 = 98 N
  f  = 0.3 × 98 = 29.4 N        the push needed before it moves
```

Static friction resists a stationary object up to a maximum and adjusts itself to whatever is
applied below that, so a block pushed with 10 N experiences 10 N of friction and stays put.
Kinetic friction acts once sliding starts and is roughly constant. The static coefficient is
larger, which is why a heavy object is harder to start than to keep moving.

Friction is non-conservative, so the energy it removes cannot be recovered by reversing the
motion. That is what puts it outside [[Conservation of Energy]] and requires the
[[Work-Energy Theorem]] to account for the loss.
